description: Well-formed queries, used to measure the form check's FALSE-REJECTION rate. Every entry here is a request a practitioner could plausibly type and the corpus could plausibly answer. The hard cases -- an acronym subject, a hyphenated subject, a gerund noun, a one-word query, a statement rather than a question, and a well-formed question that is out of the corpus's domain -- are the ones the benchmark generator's own `_subject_is_usable` filter rejects, so they are the cases where a form check built by reusing that filter would fail.
provenance: Hand-authored by the project author from the definition of 'a request that can be looked up'. The rule under test and these labels share an author, so the rate they produce is an author-label measurement, not an independent annotation. The entries are frozen here so that the measurement is reproducible and auditable: anyone can re-run the check and disagree with a label in the open.
label: valid
